final:
I checked all four review issues against the PR diff and wrote the verdicts to `verdicts.json` (it parses as valid JSON). Only one issue points at a real problem, and fixing it is optional. I didn't change any code or post any replies.

| # | Issue | Category | Verdict | Actionable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | The Postgres test skip removes coverage | BEST-PRACTICE | PARTIALLY_VALID | OPTIONAL |
| 1 | Track the resource-version short-circuit TODO | NITPICK | STYLE_PREFERENCE | NO |
| 2 | No per-key guard, so the same index can be built twice | CORRECTNESS/PERF | VALID | OPTIONAL |
| 3 | Docstring coverage is 0% | CONVENTION | INVALID | NO |

- **#0:** The skip at `pkg/server/module_server_test.go:35-38` turns the test off for every Postgres run, including local ones, even though its own message says the test "works locally." The coverage loss is real but small: it's one integration test, it has a TODO, and SQLite is already skipped the same way. Gating the skip on a CI-only env var would be an improvement, but it isn't required.
- **#1:** The PR only turns an existing TODO log line into a comment (`bleve.go:100`). Nothing new is at risk of being forgotten; whether to file a tracking issue is a process choice.
- **#2:** This is the most substantive one.
  - **What changed:** `bleve.go:137-139` now takes the lock only around the cache write, not the whole build.
  - **The gap:** `getOrCreateIndex` (`search.go:287-305`) checks the cache and then builds, with nothing stopping two callers doing that for the same key.
  - **What goes wrong:** two concurrent Search requests (`search.go:148/160`) for a namespace that has no index yet can both build it at the same time. One result overwrites the other in the cache.
  - **What makes it mild:** this gap existed before the PR too; builds just ran one at a time. It wastes work but doesn't corrupt anything, because this path builds in-memory indexes (`size=10`), so there's no fight over the same directory on disk. Startup isn't affected either: `init` builds distinct keys, and after this PR it finishes before the server starts handling requests.
  - **Fix:** a `singleflight` keyed on the namespace/resource would be cheap. The existing TODO at `search.go:288-290` already asks for this.
- **#3:** This is a generic tool threshold, not something about this diff. The PR adds no new functions, and the functions it touches already have doc comments where Go convention expects them.

The PR author's question about what might depend on lazy initialization wasn't one of the review issues, so I didn't answer it. One related finding from `init`: the search index is now fully built before the watcher starts (`server.go` Init reorder). Any live events emitted during that build window are therefore not seen by the watcher.
